arguments: Possible null pointer dereference and invalid write in operation release
message.text: Possible null pointer dereference and invalid write in operation release

properties.metisTriageReason: Verdict: tfm_crypto_operation_release dereferences and writes through its handle parameter before any local NULL check or handle-value validation. Evidence: the function reads *handle at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_alloc.c:121 and writes *handle at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_alloc.c:126, while validation of h_val occurs only afterward at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_alloc.c:128. Gap: none for the reported function body; observed call sites generally validate p_handle before passing it, but that does not contradict the unsafe callee behavior.
properties.mitigation: Check `handle == NULL` before `uint32_t h_val = *handle;` and before `*handle = ...`; return `PSA_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` on NULL. Ensure any cross-boundary parameter-copying layer also validates pointer arguments before invoking this function.
properties.reasoning: tfm_crypto_operation_release() reads from and writes to the caller-provided handle pointer without first checking whether it is NULL or otherwise valid. A NULL handle would be dereferenced immediately at line 121, and line 126 writes through the pointer before any validation. If reachable from a malformed request or untrusted caller, this can crash the secure partition and produce a denial of service. The code validates the handle value only after dereferencing the pointer, so the validation order does not protect against an invalid pointer argument.
